seen_animation: A line-drawn dolphin (black) sits at the upper right of a still scene of grey wave lines. In frames 1-4 it is tilted steeply, nose down-left and forked tail up-right, partly at the right edge. Frames 5-8 rotate it toward level while it stays at the right edge. From frame 9 it is level, nose pointing left and forked tail right, with a dorsal fin, a second small hump behind it and a hanging pectoral fin. Frames 9-16 it drifts left and slightly up, moving faster in the last frames, ending near the upper centre-right in frame 16.
seen_film: Grey rippled water seen from above. A pale, elongated swimming animal appears at the upper right edge, steeply angled up-right in frames 1-4 with only its rear visible. In frames 5-8 it levels out while staying at the right edge. In frames 9-16 it swims level toward the left and slightly upward, picking up speed, its trailing end widening, and it ends near the upper centre-right in frame 16.
named_subject: a dolphin (the doodle's fish/dolphin outline, mirrored to face left, the direction of travel)
evidence: Judged from still frames only, not playback. e.png 1-5: the drawing is tilted about 45 degrees at the upper right edge, the same angle and place as the pale animal in f.png 1-5. e.png 6-9: it rotates to level while staying at the right edge, as f.png 6-9 does. e.png 9-16: small leftward steps, matching the slow drift in f.png 9-16. e.png 17-26: larger leftward and slightly upward steps, ending at about x 360-440 of 500 in e.png 26, where the film animal sits in f.png 26. g.png shows one monotonic leftward path with the spacing widening over time and no gaps or reversals. The outline keeps the same strokes from frame to frame (dorsal fin hook, second hump, pectoral fin, forked tail), with no doubling or redraw.
primary_gap: Between e.png 20 and 25 the dorsal fin and the small hump behind it are drawn bigger and closer together than in c.png, so the top of the body reads as a cluster of overlapping strokes rather than the doodle's single clean fin.
closes_when: In e.png 17-26 the dorsal fin stays the same size and proportion as in c.png and e.png 9, with a clear gap between the fin and the small hump behind it.
protect: The tilt-then-level rotation in e.png 1-9 timed to the film; the left-moving path with slow early steps and faster later steps; the end position matching f.png 26; the doodle's sparse single-line strokes and forked tail; the static grey water lines.
identity_gap: The character is the c.png doodle mirrored horizontally, with all its strokes kept, and it reads as the same drawing; the only drift is the dorsal fin growing in the late frames.
